title: operational-roulette-kpi-scenarios-and-fallback-matrix
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is a tactical, scenario-driven KPI planner for late-stage launch decisions where traffic, latency, cost, and model-quality tradeoffs interact. It prioritizes clear thresholds, short escalation paths, and tested fallback actions so on-call and launch owners can move without debate when signals deviate.

How to read this doc (quick):
- Row-level scenarios (A–E) are traffic/KPI states we expect during first 72h of launch.
- Each scenario lists the primary metric that flips the decision, secondary supporting metrics, immediate mitigations (soft & hard), and a 3-step rollback/escalation pattern.
- Confidence bands: green/amber/red indicate how sure we are that a mitigation will work; attach owners.

Quick constraints and assumptions (context):
- Launch is a medium-latency chat feature routing to hosted Redwood models + dedicated fallback pool.
- Baseline SLOs: p95 latency <= 850ms, error rate < 0.5%, cost per 1k tokens target $X (reference in linked artifacts).
- Traffic seed: 5k DAU -> expected burst patterns: 20 req/s baseline -> 250 req/s peak in worst-case.
- Dedicated capacity reserved for baseline, hosted autoscale handles spikes.

Scenario grid (A–E):
- Scenario A: Nominal warm traffic
  - Trigger metric: sustained 10–60rps, p95 latency < 700ms, error < 0.2%
  - Supporting metrics: KV cache hit > 60%, model token utilization within expected distribution
  - Immediate mitigations: no action; enable sampling telemetry (1% full trace)
  - Confidence band: green
  - Owner: launch-ops@redwood (Samira)

- Scenario B: Early surge with slight latency drift
  - Trigger metric: spike to 120–180rps, p95 latency 700–1,000ms, error < 1%
  - Supporting: drop in KV hit ratio, increase in CPU scheduling queued requests
  - Soft mitigations (fast): increase batch window by 1–2ms, enable prefix cache for repeated prompts, temporarily reduce max_tokens to 80 for non-critical routes
  - Hard mitigations (if soft fails within 10m): divert 10% traffic to dedicated pool, enable per-route rate limiter for lowest-tier keys
  - Confidence band: amber for soft mitigations, green for hard mitigations
  - Owner rotation: infra-oncall (Ethan) primary, product-ops backup (Priya)

- Scenario C: High error amplification (model OOMs / kernel failures)
  - Trigger metric: error rate rises above 2% OR OOM alerts on >2 GPUs in 15m window
  - Supporting: model queue lengths spike, automated fallback model warmup failures
  - Immediate mitigations: auto-fallback to smaller-quantized variant for 50% traffic, pause new canary traffic, increase autoscale min replicas for dedicated pool by +1 set
  - Escalation steps: 1) Activate incident channel + SRE; 2) Execute partial rollback of feature flags for 30% of users; 3) If >2h unresolved, full rollback to previous stable route
  - Confidence band: amber (fallback variants tested in staging; possible quality regression)
  - Owners: eng-serving-runtime (Liam) primary, product-ops (Samira) communicator

- Scenario D: Quality degradation observed by eval set
  - Trigger metric: automated eval set score drop >4% relative to baseline on 10k sample or recurrent user complaint rate >0.1%
  - Supporting: increased rewording prompts, higher token count per session, manual QA notes
  - Immediate mitigations: divert to model variant with original weights (no quantization), reduce temperature with traffic split 70/30 to safe variant, freeze any ongoing rollouts
  - Confidence band: green for rollback to previous weights, amber for mixed-split traffic
  - Owners: research/applied-ml (Priya) lead, product-ops for comms

- Scenario E: Cost runaway without latency improvement
  - Trigger metric: 3x projected token spend over 6h window while p95 latency remains >800ms
  - Supporting: increased batch sizes with no latency improvement, cache miss >80%
  - Immediate mitigations: enable cost-throttle (soft) to cap tokens per user/day, scale down non-critical background jobs, switch cold-start model routing to a lower-cost variant
  - Hard mitigation: pause non-essential telemetry sampling, open emergency billing escalation thread
  - Confidence band: amber-red (cost mitigation affects product experience)
  - Owners: finance-ops (notify), infra-oncall (Ethan) execute

Decision matrix (how to pick actions quickly):
- If trigger metric breached AND supporting metrics point to capacity => prefer routing/batching/capacity mitigations before rollback.
- If trigger metric breaches with supporting metrics indicating model quality (eval drop, complaints) => prefer fallback to previous model variant or reduce exposure via canary pause.
- If multiple scenarios fire at once (e.g., C + E) => treat quality-first (protect users) then cost.

Operational playbook snippets (copyable):
- Telemetry capture checklist (1–5 mins):
  1) Check p95/p99 latency by route (last 15m) and trace tail sampler for 5 traces.
  2) Query KV cache hitrate: SELECT window_start, kv_hit_pct FROM infra.metrics WHERE route = 'chat-v1' AND window_start > now() - interval '15m';
  3) Confirm autoscale events in last 30m in infra logs; note scale up/down churn.

- Quick roll-forward (tested pattern):
  1) Apply 10% traffic split to fallback variant and watch eval score / latency for 12m.
  2) If score recovers and latency improves, increase to 50% and deprecate failing variant.
  3) If not, roll back split and execute canary rollback to prior stable route.

Staffing & rotations for first 72h:
- Launch morning (08:00–14:00): product-ops + infra-oncall + 2 SREs on pager; ML researcher on-call standby.
- Peak evening (17:00–23:00): reduced staffing but infra-oncall must be reachable; schedule 30m check-ins every 4 hours.
- Hand-offs must include a brief: current scenario letter (A–E), last mitigation actions, outstanding unknowns.

Prelaunch checklist (minimum viable gates):
- Bench: end-to-end p95 latency in staging at 80% of production traffic <= production SLO
- Backstop: validated fallback variant in staging with 1000 sample evals and human pass rate >= baseline -2%
- Billing guardrails: daily budget cap configured for feature route and notified billing contact
- Rollout flags: canary split enabled, automatic rollback policy in place, alerting for metric thresholds configured
- Runbook published linked in incident channel

Postmortem triggers (fast):
- Any full rollback of feature within first 72h
- Error rate >3% sustained for >30m
- Cost delta >200% vs simulation plan in 6h window

Notes, open questions and TODOs:
- TODO: create a synthetic probe set that mimics top-10 customer prompts for quality regressions (owner: research)
- TODO: add an automated canary observer that can flip simple mitigations without manual steps (owner: product-ops)
- Open Q: threshold sensitivity for token-capping; finance wants a safer hard threshold but product worried about UX. Please add notes to JIRA-OPS-846.
